profile.story: Marcus left a national agency in 2018 with two clients and built Northstar into a seven-person demand-generation shop running paid media, lifecycle email and revenue reporting for B2B software and services firms. The work is genuinely good and the tooling is modern — the team runs HubSpot, Asana and Looker Studio properly. What is fragile is the shape of the book: one client, a private-equity-backed logistics platform, is 38% of revenue and is up for renewal in March. Marcus is also the only person who has ever spoken to that client's CMO. He has no accountant on retainer, has never produced a P&L for anyone, and runs the business off the bank balance and a spreadsheet.

P1.note: Four sources with monthly volume and cost in HubSpot (q23: referrals 9, LinkedIn 7, inbound 4, directories 2), all marked tracked.
P1.why_not_higher: Quality is scored from memory and the tracking has never been reconciled to revenue — q30 confirms acquisition cost is never brought into the review, so cost per source exists but is not used.

P2.note: Every source creates a HubSpot deal automatically and a scheduling link goes out inside five minutes — watched firing in session. Human contact usually within a day.
P2.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs a human response under an hour; the first human touch waits on Marcus's calendar.

P3.note: A four-email sequence runs on every lead and then stops; after that, follow-up 'depends on whether I remember' (q24).
P3.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs missed follow-ups visible in the system; once the sequence ends nothing shows a lead going cold.

P4.note: HubSpot stages exist and the last twelve proposals were walked through them live; close rate 25% tracked by source (q25).
P4.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs stages used by the business, not one person — there is no written playbook and nobody but Marcus runs a deal.

P5.note: Q28: competitor-set and gut, unchanged since 2023, pricing named as a current worry. The attribution build is priced below cost by his own admission in b3.
P5.why_not_higher: Two-plus years unchanged with anecdotal reasoning is the anchor-1 line; it is not 0 only because named tiers exist and discounts are rare.

P6.note: Three named retainer tiers with a premium option, an entry-level attribution build, and a day-90 lifecycle cross-sell sequence shown running on every paid media account (q29).
P6.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs the upsell routine across the team; the cross-sell fires automatically but only Marcus ever has the conversation it creates.

P7.note: Retainer renewal roughly 80% and average tenure 26 months, both known from memory and the HubSpot deal history (q27).
P7.why_not_higher: No inactive list exists and no reactivation has ever run — anchor 3 needs the list pulled and worked.

P8.note: Monday pipeline review observed: five KPIs on a shared Looker board, three with named owners, targets visible (q39).
P8.why_not_higher: Marketing and sales are both Marcus by his own answer, and CAC is never in the review — anchor 3 needs named owners and value and cost reviewed together.

P9.note: 55% gross margin is his estimate with nothing behind it — no P&L, no account-level costing, and q17 says he can feel which accounts are unprofitable but cannot prove it.
P9.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs the overall number actually known; this one is remembered, and the CPA reconstructs it once a year at tax time.

P10.note: Q20 'inconsistent'; the QuickBooks file was opened in session and last reconciled in May. The CPA produces a tax return in April from the bank feed. No monthly P&L exists.
P10.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs monthly-ish financials however late; here there is no monthly close at all, and he looks at the bank balance instead.

S1.note: Q50 keeps pricing, major sales, escalations, hiring, banking, vendors and strategy with Marcus; the account manager decides delivery only.
S1.why_not_higher: Only routine delivery is delegated; every decision above it returns to him — anchor 2 needs several areas genuinely handed over.

S2.note: Four-week test (q51): campaigns and reporting keep running because Asana holds the work; scope decisions, pricing and invoicing stop, and the largest client's weekly call cannot be covered.
S2.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs a named deputy and only a few owner-locked items; money, new business and the biggest account are all locked.

S3.note: Marcus brought in eight of nine accounts and 80% of revenue rides on his personal relationships (q14). The account manager can scope, but has never closed or renewed.
S3.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs the team selling with owner rescue on big deals; here nobody else has ever sold anything.

S4.note: One account manager with a title and direct reports (q10); q34 says exception escalation is 'rarely' consistent and q36 lists the owner stepping in as a recurring failure.
S4.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs some real managers owning outcomes; this lead escalates rather than decides.

S5.note: Notion playbook opened live: onboarding and campaign build documented and current; quarterly review and renewal have no procedure at all. Q35 puts documented at 50% and followed at 40%.
S5.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs core workflows documented and current — the two workflows that carry renewal risk are the two that are missing.

S6.note: Weekly structured meeting (q40) observed with five KPIs and visible targets on the Looker board.
S6.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs owners on the KPIs and follow-through; two of five default to Marcus and q39 says a miss triggers a conversation rather than a change.

S7.note: Delivery quality is consistent enough that complaints are absent from q36, but q31 says a 20% jump means hiring, and the analyst is already the single point on every report.
S7.why_not_higher: No capacity plan and no defined QC step — growth currently runs on Priya's evenings.

S8.note: Largest client 38% of revenue with a March renewal; top five 79% (q14, from his own spreadsheet — no revenue-by-customer report exists to verify it).
S8.why_not_higher: Above 30% is the 0 anchor. Reported rather than Documented, which the rubric names as the single most common way concentration risk is understated.

S9.note: 74% of revenue is contracted retainers with three-month minimums renewing at ~80% (q12), all visible in the HubSpot deal records walked in session — well past the 40% line, and the retainer book is reviewed weekly.
S9.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs a forecastable base; with 38% of it renewing in one March decision, the forecast is one conversation away from being wrong.

S10.note: Client agreements and employment agreements are written (q53), but q52 names the concentration and the sole-relationship-holder risk as known and unaddressed for two years. No continuity plan.
S10.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs the contract coverage to be broad; vendor agreements, transferability and IP ownership are all unchecked, and ad billing sits on a personal login.

L1.note: HubSpot, Asana, Looker Studio, Slack, Gusto and QuickBooks cover every core area and were all walked in session (q41).
L1.why_not_higher: One significant gap: the accounting layer is four months unreconciled, so the system exists but does not function as one.

L2.note: HubSpot ↔ Slack ↔ Asana ↔ Looker connections shown working; q42 'some integrations'.
L2.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs one or two double-entry points remaining; reporting data is re-pulled by hand from every ad platform each month, which is the largest single manual join in the business.

L3.note: Q43 claims agreed KPI definitions and accurate data, but the financial half of the picture does not exist — the QuickBooks file is four months behind, so client-side numbers and money numbers cannot be put in the same sentence.
L3.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs the numbers to be mostly right after cleanup; there is one trusted report (the Looker campaign board) and nothing trustworthy on money.

L4.note: 23 h/wk inventoried (q44). Lead capture, nurture, scheduling and pacing alerts have genuinely been automated away; 9 hours of report assembly and 6 of proposal assembly remain.
L4.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs the major repetitive tasks reduced; the largest one is untouched and is growing with the client count.

L5.note: Lead capture, the four-email nurture, meeting scheduling, campaign pacing alerts and the Looker dashboards all run reliably and were shown firing (q45).
L5.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs automations across several functions owned and monitored; delivery and marketing are covered, finance and reporting are entirely manual, and nobody is named as owner of any of it.

L6.note: Q46 covers drafting, research, marketing content, sales support and reporting; Priya demonstrated two workflows she built herself for ad copy variants and report commentary.
L6.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs measured results; the workflows are real and defined but no one has ever measured what they changed, by his own answer.

L7.note: Q47 returns two of eight — someone accountable per implementation, and the team is trained. No data rules, no human-review rule, nothing measured.
L7.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs several practices applied inconsistently; here two are true and client data is already going into unapproved tools (q48).

L8.note: Q48: unclear access, ex-employees may retain access, sensitive data in unapproved tools, and ad platform billing under Marcus's personal login (b5).
L8.why_not_higher: Anchor 2 needs partial hygiene with known gaps; ex-employee access has never been reviewed at all, which leaves this at individual-logins-and-assumptions.

L9.note: Q58 'trained, adopting, and improving it themselves' — corroborated by Priya's two self-built workflows and the media buyer acting on a pacing alert unprompted.
L9.why_not_higher: Anchor 4 needs the improvement to stick; q59 says the team adopts readily and documents nothing, so what they build does not survive them.

L10.note: Q49: $10–20K but it must come out of cash flow, 5 owner hours and 8 team hours; q55 'ready if priorities stay tight'.
L10.why_not_higher: Anchor 3 needs budget and time named and set aside; the budget is conditional on a cash position nobody is measuring monthly.

assessment.owner_objective: Resilience/risk reduction — then Reliable revenue growth, More profit & cash flow
assessment.owner_belief: The whole thing rests on one account. If the logistics client leaves in March we lose 38% of revenue in one email and I have no idea whether we'd survive it. I've known that for two years and I keep not fixing it because that client is also the one that takes the most of my time.
assessment.primary_constraint: New business capacity is one calendar: Marcus is the only person who has ever sold, renewed or held a client relationship, so the concentration he correctly fears cannot be diluted at the rate it would take to matter before March.
assessment.constraint_symptoms: Eight of nine accounts were brought in by him and 80% of revenue rides on his relationships; the largest client will not take its weekly call from anyone else; new business stops entirely in the four-week test; proposal assembly is six of his own hours a week; retainer pricing has not moved since 2023 because repricing means nine conversations only he can have.
assessment.constraint_cost: ~$418K of revenue exposed to one March renewal conversation only he can have · ~$22K of delivery payroll on nine weekly hours of report assembly · ~312 owner hours a year on proposals and invoicing.
assessment.constraint_fix: A second relationship holder inside the top three accounts within 90 days — account manager on every call, named in the renewal, and running two of the quarterly reviews — plus a written renewal and repricing procedure so the conversation stops being a personal performance.
assessment.momentum_initiative: Reprice the attribution build, which he already believes sells below cost, and put a floor under the three retainer tiers — one decision, no new hire, measurable on the next two proposals.

opportunities.title: Close more of the proposals already being written
opportunities.finding: 25% of proposals close on roughly $1.05M of proposal volume a year (HubSpot deal history, walked in session). Stages exist but no playbook does, nobody but Marcus runs a deal, and the loss reason he names is price or an in-house hire — both of which are answerable in the proposal itself. Every figure behind this rests on his own numbers: there is no P&L and no account-level costing.
opportunities.blueprint: A written proposal playbook with a costed scope model, a standard in-house-versus-agency comparison page, and the account manager on every second call so a second person can carry the deal.
opportunities.replaces: A proposal rebuilt from scratch by the owner every time

opportunities.title: Reprice the retainer tiers and put a floor under the attribution build
opportunities.finding: Retainer prices have not moved since 2023 and are set against two competitors' published rates (q28). The attribution build — 16% of revenue and the entry point for most accounts — is priced below cost by his own account in b3, and the 49% margin he wrote in q13 is a guess because nothing is costed by client. Basis is reported only: no P&L, no job costing.
opportunities.blueprint: Cost the delivery hours per account from the loaded rates in q56, set tier floors from that, and stage the increases at each renewal date rather than all at once — with the March account handled last, not first.
opportunities.replaces: Prices set by reading two competitors' websites in 2023

opportunities.title: Automate the monthly client reporting assembly
opportunities.finding: Priya spends nine hours a week — demonstrated live at three hours ten minutes for one client — pulling platform data, screenshotting and hand-writing commentary into slides. The Looker dashboards already hold the data; the manual work is the assembly and the narrative. Those hours go straight back onto billable delivery, which is why they are being counted as dollars rather than capacity.
opportunities.blueprint: Scheduled Looker exports into a templated report, AI-drafted commentary from the campaign data with the analyst reviewing and signing rather than writing, and the client-facing deck generated rather than assembled.
opportunities.replaces: Three hours of screenshots per client per month
